chapter_title: Chương 299: 0301 [Bốn mươi năm sau sẽ ra sao?]

segments.title: Chương 299: 0301 [Bốn mươi năm sau sẽ ra sao?]
segments.content:
A single stock market commentary post on Daitou Dage 777's blog could easily get over 500,000 views in a single day.

He set up many QQ groups, all requiring a membership fee to join.

The fees ranged from a minimum of 3,000 yuan per year to a maximum of 37,000 yuan per year, and he even created customer tiers like Gold, Platinum, and Diamond.

The guy was already in a bind, and after being blasted by Wu Yue San Ren, he took the opportunity to announce his retirement. He claimed he was the target of envy and jealousy, and that daily harassment had made it impossible for him to live a normal life.

The last stock he recommended hit its daily limit up the very next day.

His influence was so great that not only did many retail investors listen to him, but even some institutional investors had infiltrated his QQ groups. Whenever he said a certain stock would rise, everyone would flock to buy it.

It would've been strange if it didn't rise!

But this guy wasn't getting away. He was already on the radar of the relevant authorities.

If he had only been recommending stocks, it wouldn't have been a big deal, but collecting membership fees for it would surely land him in jail.

Wu Yue San Ren successfully diverted the netizens' attention. With Daitou Dage 777's retirement, all his stock-investing fans flocked over to curse him out, believing that Wu Yue San Ren had cut off their path to riches.

This was exactly the effect Wu Yue San Ren wanted. He argued with those stock investors day in and day out, and finally, no one was scrutinizing his academic qualifications anymore.

He knew he would definitely win, because he had already reported him.

Chen Guiliang, on the other hand, came out of this whole affair unscathed. In fact, it even brought attention to "My Own Swordsman."

Even Director Kou from the Publication Administration personally called: "For this year's list of National Online Game Projects, Youke only submitted 'Future Era.' Do you want to submit 'My Own Swordsman' as well?"

Chen Guiliang said: "We haven't even started making 'My Own Swordsman' yet. We're just in the early preparatory stages."

"As long as the project has been established, it's fine," Director Kou said. "I've seen the preparatory work you've done, holding classes at Tsinghua and Peking University, conducting on-site research. This kind of spirit is worthy of commendation. Moreover, it contains historical and cultural elements that can change the public's perception of online games."

Director Kou saw things from a different perspective. He didn't even care that much whether a game was profitable or not.

For example, "Voyage Century," which he once supported, was because the game told a patriotic story about a group of overseas Chinese in the early 16th century who returned east after enduring all sorts of hardships, their blood boiling with passion. At the same time, it showcased the clash of Eastern and Western civilizations and promoted China's five-thousand-year-long history.

The above was pure nonsense. To put it bluntly, it was just an online version of "Uncharted Waters."

But Director Kou loved to hear these kinds of stories!

He was also very fond of games like "Demi-Gods and Semi-Devils," trying to use them to promote the "export of Chinese martial arts culture."

"Demi-Gods and Semi-Devils" had just started development, and no one even knew what it would look like, yet it was already added to the list of National Online Game Projects by the Publication Administration.

Director Kou said: "I won't rush you on 'My Own Swordsman.' Just take your time and do it well. You can come to the Publication Administration to apply for a publication number when the time comes."

"Thank you for your support, leader," Chen Guiliang said happily.

The game publication number system was already in place, and could even be traced back to 2004.

But supervision wasn't strict.

Three departments—the Publication Administration, the Ministry of Culture, and the Ministry of Information Industry—all had the authority to approve game publication numbers.

Theoretically, all three departments needed to approve it, but in practice, a nod from just one of them was enough.

Many small and medium-sized game companies even dared to launch without a publication number. And surprisingly, no one bothered them. Because all three departments could regulate it, it often ended up with no one bothering to regulate it at all.

Director Kou asking "My Own Swordsman" to submit to the Publication Administration was his way of securing the claim on this excellent game in advance. He was worried that the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of Information Industry would try to snatch the credit later on!

This year, the publication number for "World of Warcraft" was going to be re-examined because the new expansion pack contained a lot of red and gold (especially the Shattered Sun Offensive emblem).

Things like gore and superstition were secondary. The main issue was those two colors, which had to be changed before the Olympics.

It was a small matter, a simple change would suffice.

But The9's attitude was extremely arrogant, or rather, it had become inflated beyond measure. Not only did they drag their feet on the changes, they also claimed the Publication Administration's review process was inefficient, inciting players to create public opinion and threaten the administration.

The more uncooperative The9 was, the more changes the Publication Administration demanded. And it was always a case of, once you've made the changes, I'll come up with new requirements.

And how did NetEase get the publication number to be the new operator for "World of Warcraft"? They bypassed the Publication Administration entirely and had the Ministry of Culture approve it!

The Publication Administration was instantly enraged. This was a game I had previously approved and demanded corrections for. What do you mean by bypassing me and issuing a publication number directly?

Are you trying to switch allegiances?

Thus, the Publication Administration unilaterally declared the publication number invalid.

The Publication Administration and the Ministry of Culture started fighting directly. The central government saw this couldn't continue and proceeded to standardize the responsibilities and powers of each department. It was also from this point on that the regulation of game publication numbers became stricter.

When Chen Guiliang had just said "Thank you for your support, leader," the emphasis wasn't on the literal meaning, but on expressing that he would always follow the Publication Administration. He was determined not to align with the camps of the Ministry of Culture or the Ministry of Information Industry.

"If 'My Own Swordsman' is submitted this year, can it be selected along with 'Future Era'?" Chen Guiliang inquired.

Director Kou replied: "Not this year. I can't select two games from the same company at once. But there's a chance next year, which is why I'm telling you to submit it in advance."

Chen Guiliang expressed his understanding.

Director Kou added: "You sent me a closed beta invitation code a few days ago, and I've personally played 'Future Era.' It's very good. Although there are only two chapters and the max level is only 25, the game's story is particularly well done. Its spiritual core is positive and uplifting, showing humanity united and willing to sacrifice when facing a crisis. This isn't promoting violence, but encouraging a spirit of striving and struggle."

Chen Guiliang almost laughed. "Leaders really are on another level, seeing things from a broader perspective."

Director Kou continued his evaluation: "The fatigue system is also a great feature. It's a design to prevent addiction. If teenagers play the game, the depletion of their fatigue points will make them stop. If 'Future Era' can be updated with a few more maps, I will recommend this game to foreign companies at this year's ChinaJoy."

"Chapter Two's development started last December, and it was actually almost finished before the Spring Festival. We've currently completed two dungeons for Chapter Three. By summer vacation, we can definitely update to Chapter Four, with a character level cap of 45," Chen Guiliang said.

After a bit more small talk, the call ended.

Chen Guiliang sat at his computer and went to 17173 to check the rankings.

"Future Era" currently only had 3,000 players in its closed beta, with the highest character level being 25.

Even as an unfinished product, it had shot straight to 18th on the weekly online game chart and 2nd on the new online games chart (1st place was "Demi-Gods and Semi-Devils").

Several editors gave it a five-star recommendation, unanimously agreeing that all the time spent had not been in vain.

One editor even said: "The level design in 'Future Era' has the quality of a premium single-player game. It tells a complete story, with a fully developed worldview and plotline. This is extremely rare in online games."

The praise was very high.

Back at the dorm, Tong Zhihong was playing "Future Era," while Li Heng was practicing a speech in front of the mirror.

"What are you doing?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Li Heng explained: "I'm preparing for the speech competition. This year's theme is 'Envisioning 2048.' 2048 is the 150th anniversary of Peking University, the 99th anniversary of the founding of New China, and the 40th anniversary of the Beijing Olympics. What will China and Peking University be like then?"

Chen Guiliang smiled: "That's an interesting theme."

"I joined because I thought the theme was interesting," Li Heng said, envisioning the future. "By 2048, cars, computers, and mobile phones will definitely be widespread in China. The Western Development program will be complete, and people in both the east and west will be prosperous. Beijing will no longer have sandstorms, and the grassland restoration will be a great success. By then, China's GDP will be the second largest in the world, second only to the United States..."

"Also, thanks to great technological advancements, poverty will have been eliminated in all countries and regions around the world. Humanity will no longer wage wars over resources, and the United Nations will become increasingly authoritative. Even the US won't dare to openly violate UN documents anymore..."

The fellow went on and on, all optimistic and positive.

Chen Guiliang didn't pour cold water on him. It was good to maintain such an optimistic attitude.

But Li Heng took the initiative to ask: "What's your vision of 2048?"

Chen Guiliang said: "World War III might be over by then."

"Huh?"

Even Tong Zhihong, who was playing his game, whipped his head around.

Chen Guiliang smiled: "Just a wild guess, no need to be shocked."

Tong Zhihong said: "If there's a World War III, with all that stuff being thrown around, the Earth would be blasted into a real-life 'Future Era.' And there won't be any spiritual energy revival then."
